agenda: Reports of the Secretary-General on the Sudan and South Sudan
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: The United States aims to renew UNMISS while responding firmly to the Nasir clashes, prioritizing civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and credible electoral preparations. The main difficulties will be balancing robust Chapter VII language and accountability demands with sovereignty concerns from Russia and China, and ensuring the Government of South Sudan accepts strong language on cooperation and human rights. The draft is designed to keep traditional UNMISS language that can attract at least nine votes while isolating any veto risk.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of UNMISS and the priority attached to protection of civilians. We ask the penholder to remove the call for full implementation of the arms embargo and instead reflect that sanctions should remain under review in light of progress in transitional security arrangements. We also need explicit operative language on respect for South Sudan's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national ownership, with close consultation with the Government and reference to African Union and IGAD support. Accountability should be pursued in a manner that respects national jurisdiction.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNMISS and its core mandate to protect civilians and facilitate humanitarian access. However, the text should better reflect South Sudan's sovereignty and national ownership, avoid prejudging the sanctions measures in resolution 2731, and frame accountability in accordance with national law. We also call for explicit reference to the African Union and IGAD and for election-related support to be clearly led by South Sudan and based on the consent of the parties.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the renewal of UNMISS with a robust mandate to protect civilians and ensure humanitarian access. We would like the text to reflect the women, peace and security agenda more explicitly, especially women’s and youth participation in political and electoral processes, and to strengthen language on removing bureaucratic impediments to humanitarian access. We also suggest that reporting include WPS implementation so the Council can track progress.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of UNMISS and welcomes the United States draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text on robust protection of civilians, compliance with the Status of Forces Agreement, accountability for conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children, and women’s participation. These changes are important for the credibility and operational effectiveness of the mandate, and we are ready to engage constructively.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of UNMISS and the draft's robust protection-of-civilians, humanitarian-access and accountability provisions. We ask that the text explicitly reflect the women, peace and security and children and armed conflict agendas, including in the mandate and reporting, and that OP7 name women, youth and persons with disabilities in the political process. We would also welcome a preambular reference to climate-related security risks. These changes would strengthen the text without altering its core.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of UNMISS and welcomes the draft’s focus on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 on removing bureaucratic impediments to humanitarian access, OP6 on Government cooperation with accountability mechanisms, and OP7 on the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women and youth. These changes would reinforce the Council’s response to the recent clashes in Nasir and the broader political and humanitarian crisis.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of UNMISS and shares the draft’s concern at the clashes in Nasir and the humanitarian situation. As a major troop- and police-contributing country, we ask the penholder to ensure that any review or reconfiguration of UNMISS is undertaken in close consultation with T/PCCs and the host Government and that reporting includes the safety and security of peacekeepers. We also seek explicit reference to national ownership in UNMISS support for elections, consistent with South Sudan’s sovereignty.
messages.Panama: Panama strongly supports the renewal of UNMISS and the draft’s robust protection-of-civilians and accountability language. We would like the text to reflect the Council’s women, peace and security and youth, peace and security commitments more explicitly, including in support for elections and constitution-making, and to ensure humanitarian access is described as rapid as well as safe and unhindered. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of UNMISS and commends the United States for a comprehensive draft. We would like the reporting requirements to explicitly cover arms embargo violations and the humanitarian access language to address bureaucratic impediments. We also ask for standard WPS language on the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in the political process and elections.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of UNMISS and remains committed to the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of South Sudan. We cannot accept language that turns the Mission into an instrument of external pressure on the host Government or that prejudges the outcome of national investigations. We therefore propose the amendments above and expect the penholder to reflect these concerns; otherwise we will have to abstain.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of UNMISS and a robust protection-of-civilians mandate. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text on women's and youth participation, child protection, and accountability for grave violations, including the recruitment and use of children and conflict-related sexual violence. With these adjustments, we are ready to support the draft.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of UNMISS and welcomes the robust protection and accountability language in the draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP2(a) with gender-responsive protection and child protection, OP5 with cross-line and cross-border access and removal of arbitrary impediments, OP7 with women’s, youth, and civil society participation, and OP8 reporting on access obstruction and child rights violations. These changes are important for a mandate that reflects the situation on the ground and Slovenia’s consistent position on protection and accountability.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of UNMISS and the draft's strong focus on protection of civilians, humanitarian access and accountability. As an IGAD member and African elected member, we ask the penholder to add clear references to the African Union and IGAD and to ensure UNMISS coordination with regional mechanisms, including in reporting. These changes would strengthen regional ownership and do not weaken the mandate.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate and thanks the United States for its penholdership. We would like the text to explicitly require the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth in the political process and elections, and to strengthen reporting on women, peace and security and child protection. We also ask that OP5 reflect rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access, including across conflict lines and borders, and that OP6 explicitly include conflict-related sexual violence in the accountability demands.

steps.summary: The revised draft preserves the core US priorities of a robust UNMISS mandate, protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability, and the arms embargo while accommodating many sovereignty, regional, WPS, and reporting requests. It should attract broad support, with China and Russia likely abstaining rather than blocking renewal.

messages.Algeria: We thank the penholder for incorporating sovereignty, national jurisdiction and AU/IGAD language. Our remaining concern is PP9: as the A3+ has consistently stated, the South Sudan sanctions regime, particularly the arms embargo, should be kept under review with a view to adjustment in light of progress on transitional security. We request the replacement above and can support the renewal of UNMISS.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for accommodating several of our proposals. We continue to believe that the text should avoid prejudging the sanctions and arms embargo and should ensure accountability language respects South Sudan’s national jurisdiction. We request the adjustments in PP9 and OP6, and a minor refinement in OP7. With these changes, China is prepared to support the renewal of UNMISS.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on women, peace and security, youth participation, humanitarian access and reporting. We support the current text and believe it provides a robust mandate for UNMISS to protect civilians, facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access and support inclusive political processes. Denmark calls on all parties to cooperate fully with UNMISS and urges swift adoption of the resolution.
messages.France: France supports the revised draft and thanks the United States for incorporating the priorities we raised in the previous round. The text sends a clear message on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability, and women’s participation. France calls for its swift adoption and urges all parties, including the Government of South Sudan, to comply fully with their obligations, including under the Status of Forces Agreement.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our priorities on women, peace and security, children and armed conflict, disability inclusion, and climate-related risk. The text strikes a balanced approach between a robust protection mandate and respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty. Greece encourages full implementation of the mandate and continued reporting on accountability, humanitarian access, and the situation in Upper Nile.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for accepting our proposed language on humanitarian access, accountability cooperation, and women and youth participation. With those revisions reflected, Guyana supports the current draft as a balanced basis for renewing UNMISS’s mandate. We urge all Council members to join consensus, while stressing that implementation, especially on access to Nasir and other conflict-affected areas and the protection of civilians, must remain the Council’s focus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the current draft. Our previous concerns on South Sudan’s sovereignty and national ownership, close consultation with troop- and police-contributing countries and the Government of South Sudan, and reporting on peacekeeper safety have been reflected. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and adopt the text.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes the revised text and the incorporation of its priorities on women, youth and civil society participation and on rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We believe the draft provides a robust and balanced mandate for UNMISS and a clear message on cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians and accountability. Panama supports the text as it stands and will vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier suggestions on arms embargo reporting, removal of bureaucratic impediments, and women and youth participation. UNMISS must continue to protect civilians and facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, especially in Upper Nile. We encourage the Council to unite behind the text so that the mandate can be renewed without delay.
messages.Russian Federation: We welcome the partial incorporation of our proposals, but the text still does not fully reflect the host State’s primary responsibility and continues to use language that could turn UNMISS into a tool of external pressure. We therefore cannot support the draft as it stands and ask for the remaining changes on OP2(a), OP3, OP6 and the arms embargo paragraph. With those adjustments, the Russian Federation is prepared to support the extension of UNMISS.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft and will vote in favour. We thank the penholder for incorporating our priorities on women, youth and civil society participation, child protection, conflict-related sexual violence and gender-based violence. We encourage robust implementation of the mandate, in close coordination with the African Union and IGAD, and in full respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty and national ownership.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text and thanks the penholder for incorporating our priorities on gender-responsive child protection, cross-line and cross-border humanitarian access, participation, and reporting on access obstructions and child rights violations. We believe the draft provides a balanced and credible basis for renewing UNMISS and responding to the recent clashes in Nasir and Upper Nile State. Slovenia encourages all Council members to support the text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on the role of the African Union and IGAD, as well as reporting on regional impact. We support the current text and encourage the Council to adopt it as a consensus renewal of the UNMISS mandate, with continued attention to African ownership and regional stability.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the revised text and the incorporation of our earlier proposals on WPS and youth participation, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access across conflict lines and borders, CRSV accountability, and WPS/child protection reporting. We support the text as it stands and call for its adoption. We urge all parties to cease hostilities, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and be held accountable for violations.

steps.summary: The revision meets Russia’s OP3 red line through host-state coordination and primary-responsibility language, while preserving robust civilian protection, humanitarian access, and independent accountability. It partially accommodates China and Algeria on national investigations, national conditions, and sanctions review, but retains full implementation and international accountability mechanisms. With broad support among Council members, the text is expected to pass despite likely abstentions by China and Russia.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria supported the draft with changes and its key concern on sanctions review was partially accommodated, so it would vote in favour while explaining sovereignty and African-led implementation priorities. The pre-vote statement reinforces those points without opposing the mandate extension.
reasons.China: China’s important requests on the arms embargo and independent accountability were not fully accepted, and its record on the substantive UNMISS renewal in 2024 was to abstain. It will not block the mission but will signal concerns by abstaining.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supports renewing UNMISS’s mandate and the draft reflects its priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and women, peace and security. There is no reason for Denmark to oppose or abstain.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and the draft aligns with its priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and South Sudan’s sovereignty and regional cooperation. No requested changes remain, so France votes in favour.
reasons.Greece: Greece supports UN peacekeeping mandates that prioritize civilian protection and humanitarian access, and the draft retains key WPS, children, disability and climate-risk language consistent with Greek positions. No Greek interest or prior commitment requires abstention or opposition.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana’s last negotiation position was support with no requested changes, and it has consistently backed UNMISS renewal while emphasizing sovereignty, humanitarian access, accountability and inclusion. A brief pre-vote explanation is consistent with that policy.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft in negotiations, has no requests, and generally backs UNMISS mandate renewals emphasizing peacekeeper safety, sovereignty, and civilian protection. The vote is therefore in favour.
reasons.Panama: Panama had already expressed support and sought no changes; the draft aligns with Panama’s consistent support for UNMISS, civilian protection, humanitarian access and South Sudanese sovereignty.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and the draft retains key priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and arms-embargo reporting. Voting in favour aligns with ROK’s established position and no changes were requested in the last negotiation round.
reasons.Russian Federation: The OP3 red line on host-state coordination and South Sudan's primary responsibility to protect civilians was accommodated. UNMISS renewal is critical amid recent clashes, and remaining concerns over accountability and arms embargo language do not justify abstention or veto.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supported the draft in negotiations and has no outstanding requests; the text retains protection-of-civilians, WPS, child protection, and CRSV priorities while affirming South Sudan’s sovereignty. A favourable vote is consistent with its record and A3+ emphasis on UNMISS, humanitarian access, and regional mediation.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia is a consistent supporter of UNMISS and has prioritized protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability and gender-responsive language; the draft reflects those priorities and Slovenia requested no changes.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports UN peacekeeping renewals and had already supported this draft without requesting changes, with its concerns on sovereignty, AU/IGAD roles and regional impact reflected. Voting in favour is consistent with Somalia’s stated position and regional stability interests.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft reflects UK priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, WPS, and implementation of the peace agreement, and the UK was recorded as supporting it without requested changes. Voting in favour is consistent with the UK’s record on UNMISS and South Sudan.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and has consistently supported renewing UNMISS’s mandate, emphasizing civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and South Sudan’s political transition. The draft aligns with established U.S. policy and interests, so the United States votes yes.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of UNMISS and its essential role in protecting civilians, facilitating humanitarian access, and supporting the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement. At the same time, we stress that the Council’s action must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national ownership of South Sudan, with the African Union and IGAD playing a central role in support of the country’s political process. We take note that our request for a review of the sanctions measures with a view to adjusting them as appropriate was partially reflected, and we reiterate the importance of keeping these measures under review in light of progress on transitional security arrangements and implementation of the Revitalized Agreement. We also deplore the recent clashes in Nasir and call on all parties to cease hostilities and to ensure accountability consistent with national law and applicable international obligations.
before.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for its penholder efforts. We will vote in favour of this resolution because it renews UNMISS’s vital mandate to protect civilians, facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and support implementation of the Revitalized Agreement. Denmark remains deeply concerned by the recent clashes in and around Nasir and calls on all parties to cease hostilities, protect civilians, and ensure accountability for violations. We also stress the importance of the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth and of credible preparations for elections, and we will continue to support UNMISS and the people of South Sudan.
before.France: France welcomes the presentation of this draft resolution and thanks the United States for its work. The situation in South Sudan, particularly the recent clashes in and around Nasir and the continuing humanitarian and security challenges, demands a clear and unified message from this Council. France supports the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate so that the Mission can continue to protect civilians, facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access, monitor and report on violations, and support the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement in close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. We also stress the importance of accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights abuses, and of ensuring the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in political and electoral processes. France will vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate and its focus on protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, accountability, and the full and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. We are gravely concerned by the recent clashes in Nasir and Upper Nile State, and we call on all parties to cease hostilities, respect South Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, cooperate fully with UNMISS, and implement the Revitalized Agreement in close coordination with the African Union and IGAD.
before.Guyana: Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana thanks the United States for its work as penholder and will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate, including its protection-of-civilians responsibilities, and stress the need for full respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for the recent clashes in Nasir and all violations, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society in the political process. We call on all parties to cease hostilities and to implement the Revitalized Agreement in good faith.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate, including its focus on the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and support for the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement. As a major troop- and police-contributing country, Pakistan stresses the importance of close consultation with troop- and police-contributing countries, the safety and security of peacekeepers, and full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and national ownership of South Sudan. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, particularly in Nasir and Upper Nile State, and to cooperate fully with UNMISS and humanitarian actors.
before.Panama: Panama votes in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate because the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and support for the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement remain essential. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, including in Nasir and Upper Nile State, to protect civilians, and to ensure accountability for violations. Panama stresses full respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, and the need for national ownership, while underscoring that UNMISS must receive the necessary access and cooperation to fulfil its mandate, including with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate, including its civilian-protection responsibilities, and underline the need for safe and unhindered humanitarian access, full implementation of the Revitalized Agreement, accountability for the recent clashes in Nasir and all violations, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. We also welcome continued reporting on arms-embargo violations and stress the importance of the safety and security of UNMISS personnel and humanitarian actors. We urge all parties to cease hostilities and return to dialogue.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this resolution. Extending UNMISS is essential to protect civilians under imminent threat, especially in Upper Nile and Jonglei, and to support safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access. We welcome the resolution’s focus on accountability, conflict-related sexual violence, protection of children, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, including in and around Nasir, protect civilians, cooperate fully with UNMISS, and implement the Revitalized Agreement in good faith.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate with a clear focus on the protection of civilians and safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, particularly in Upper Nile State. We stress the central role of the African Union and IGAD, full respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and the need for an inclusive political process leading to credible elections. Somalia also welcomes the reporting on regional impact, including refugee flows and cross-border security, and calls on all parties to cease hostilities and cooperate fully with UNMISS.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, President. The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the recent clashes in and around Nasir and by the continued suffering of civilians across South Sudan. This resolution sends a clear message on the need to protect civilians, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, end conflict-related sexual violence, hold perpetrators accountable, and implement the Revitalized Agreement, including credible preparations for elections. We call on all parties to cease hostilities immediately and to cooperate fully with UNMISS. We thank the United States for its leadership.
before.United States of America: The United States strongly supports this draft resolution and calls for its adoption. The renewal of UNMISS’s mandate is essential to protecting civilians amid the recent clashes in Nasir and Upper Nile State, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and supporting South Sudan’s implementation of the Revitalized Agreement. We urge all parties to cease hostilities immediately, protect civilians, allow UNMISS and humanitarian actors to operate freely, and pursue dialogue through existing mechanisms. The United States remains committed to South Sudan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, and national unity, and to a peaceful, inclusive political transition, including credible preparations for elections with the full and meaningful participation of women, youth, and civil society. We demand accountability for attacks on civilians, humanitarian personnel, and UN personnel, and we call on the Government of South Sudan and all armed groups to engage in good faith to end the violence and address the humanitarian crisis.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China abstained in the voting on the draft resolution just adopted on the renewal of the mandate of UNMISS.

China supports the renewal of UNMISS and recognizes its important role in protecting civilians, facilitating safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and supporting the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement. We remain deeply concerned about the recent clashes in and around Nasir and Upper Nile State and call on all parties to cease hostilities, protect civilians, and ensure humanitarian access. We also support South Sudan’s efforts to advance the political transition and prepare for elections in accordance with its national conditions.

At the same time, China believes that the action of the Security Council must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan and must respect the primary responsibility of the Government of South Sudan. The draft did not fully reflect the legitimate concerns of the host country and relevant regional countries, nor did it fully incorporate the constructive proposals made during consultations, including on the central role of the African Union and IGAD, the sequencing of transitional security arrangements, and the review of sanctions measures, including the arms embargo. The mandate of UNMISS should be implemented in close consultation with the Government of South Sudan and with the full consideration of troop- and police-contributing countries. China therefore abstained.

China will continue to support an African-led and South Sudanese-owned political process and to play a constructive role in promoting peace, security and development in South Sudan.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We support the continuation of UNMISS’s activities, because the situation in South Sudan, including the recent clashes in and around Nasir and Upper Nile State, requires a stabilising presence and safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access. We call on all parties to cease hostilities and return to dialogue within the framework of the Revitalized Agreement.

At the same time, we wish to record our principled position. The mandate of UNMISS must be implemented in strict respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and for the primary responsibility of its Government. The Mission must act in close coordination with the South Sudanese authorities and in accordance with the Status of Forces Agreement. Its activities must not serve as an instrument of outside pressure or interference in internal affairs, including in the electoral process. The central role of the African Union and IGAD must be preserved.

We also reiterate that sanctions measures, including the arms embargo, should be kept under review with a view to adjusting them as progress is achieved. Restrictive measures must not become an end in themselves. We expect the Secretary-General to ensure balanced, objective and credible reporting within the approved mandate.

We thank the United States for its work as penholder. Not all of our proposals were fully reflected, but the resolution as a whole is acceptable. We voted in favour in the interests of maintaining UNMISS’s uninterrupted operation and supporting peace and stability in South Sudan.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone welcomes the adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of UNMISS until 30 April 2026. We voted in favour because the Mission continues to play an indispensable role in protecting civilians, facilitating safe and unhindered humanitarian access, monitoring and reporting on violations, and supporting the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement.

We remain gravely concerned by the recent clashes in and around Nasir and by the continued violence and humanitarian suffering in South Sudan. We call on all parties to cease hostilities immediately, protect civilians, ensure the safety and security of United Nations and humanitarian personnel, and cooperate fully with UNMISS. The sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan must be fully respected, and the primary responsibility for protecting its population rests with the Government of South Sudan.

Sierra Leone also underlines the central role of the African Union and IGAD in supporting an inclusive political process and credible preparations for elections, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. Accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights abuses, including conflict-related sexual violence, must be pursued. We further note the importance of keeping the sanctions measures under review in light of progress in implementation of the Revitalized Agreement and transitional security arrangements. Sierra Leone will continue to support the people and Government of South Sudan in their pursuit of peace, stability and development.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of UNMISS until 30 April 2026. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and for the broad support this text received today. This Council has sent a clear message that UNMISS must be able to continue its vital work: protecting civilians, facilitating safe and unhindered humanitarian access, monitoring and reporting violations, and supporting implementation of the Revitalized Agreement.

We remain gravely concerned by the recent clashes in and around Nasir and Upper Nile State, and by continuing violence and suffering across South Sudan. We call on all parties to cease hostilities immediately, protect civilians, ensure accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights abuses, and cooperate fully with UNMISS and humanitarian actors.

The United States remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan. We urge the parties to make tangible progress on transitional security arrangements, constitution-making and credible preparations for elections, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. The United States will continue to work with this Council, the African Union, IGAD and the South Sudanese people in support of a peaceful and inclusive political transition.
